text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- Marina Dropulic of ruling Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) is voted mayor of Zagreb, while Zlatko Canjuga (HDZ) becomes president of the Zagreb city Assembly.
- Some 150,000 Yugoslav dinars are exchanged for kuna during the first of three days envisaged for the currency swap in Eastern Slavonia.
- Croatia and Romania to sign an agreement on free trade later this year.
- Hrvatska Postanska Banka may be chosen as the bank to process the state pension fund, which would facilitate monthly pension payments.

- Croatian Peasants' Party (HSS) leader Zlatko Tomcic suspends HSS Zagreb city Assembly deputies Antun Sporer and Damir Bukovic for going against party policy and voting in favour of an HDZ Zagreb city Assembly president.
- The findings of Steingenberger Consulting show prices of food, drinks and other products in Croatia are more expensive than in most other tourist destinations in Europe.
- Road safety: The roads in the Podravina region are the safest, while those running through Dalmatia are the most dangerous.
- Only 5,000 package tours out of a planned 30,000 were sold to British tourists for the upcoming season. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
